question:
This is a question about dbt + jinja syntax in macro calls and defining this in a schema.yml/properties.yml model file.

I have a working macro definition and inline post-hook config in a model. It applies dbt tags to materialized models in the db (databricks in this case but not important.) It successfully works as an inline config block, when I run the model the table gets tagged in databricks. However, this is failing when I instead define the post-hook in the .yml file.

Here is the macro:

{% macro apply_dbt_tags(relation, tag_list) -%}

    ALTER TABLE {{ relation }} SET TAGS (
        {% for tag in tag_list -%}
            '{{ tag }}' {%- if not loop.last %}, {% endif -%}
        {%- endfor %}
    )

{%- endmacro -%}

Here is the model file (this inline config block works correctly):

-- demo_apply_tags.sql

{{
  config(
    post_hook = "{{ apply_dbt_tags(this, model.config.tags) }}"
    )
}}
select
    'hello there' col1
    , 'general kenobi' col2

The model properties file:

version: 2

models:
  - name: demo_apply_tags
    description: "attempt to apply the tags of this model to the dbx table"
    config:
      tags: ["obi", "wan"]

So I run it,

dbt run --model demo_apply_tags

# now I go to the cloud db console and see the tags are attached to the new table.

I want to move the post_hook definition to the properties file:

models:
  - name: demo_apply_tags
    description: 2nd attempt to apply new tags
    config:
      tags: ["ewoks", "were misused"]
    post_hook: "{{ apply_dbt_tags(this, model.config.tags) }}"

# Compilation Error
#   Could not render {{ apply_dbt_tags(this, model.config.tags) }}: 'model' is undefined

Update 1/n

So going by the documentation in v1.8.5 the above is incorrect as post_hook is a part of the config and should indent one more level in. I also simplified things by refactoring to remove the arguments, as the macro can glean the model and tags from the context (model.config.tags, this):

Exhibit 1A still unsolved

# l ./models/demo/properties.yml

models:
  - name: demo_apply_tags
    description: 2nd attempt to apply the tags of this model to the dbx table
    config:
      tags: ["use", "force"]
      post_hook: "{{ apply_dbt_tags() }}"

$> dbt run --model demo_apply_tags
# Compilation Error
  # Could not render {{ apply_dbt_tags() }}: 'apply_dbt_tags' is undefined

I swear, the above looks to me exactly like the documentation.

FYI simpler 0-arg macro definition:

{% macro apply_dbt_tags() -%}
    {% set tags_list = model.config.tags %}
    ALTER TABLE {{ this }} SET TAGS (
        {% for tag in tags_list -%}
            '{{ tag }}' {%- if not loop.last %}, {% endif -%}
        {%- endfor %}
    )d
{%- endmacro -%}

Working Solution

Anyway, this works at the top level:

# dbt_project.yml
models:
  muh_project:
    demo:
      schema: muh_demo
      materialized: table
      +tags: ['demo', 'kamino']
      +post-hook: "{{ apply_dbt_tags() }}"

The post hook applies those tags to all tables in the models/demo folder, as well as the tags defined in model config in models/demo/properties.yml.

-- databricks SQL
select *
from system.information_schema.table_tags
where catalog_name = 'muh_catalog' and schema_name = 'muh_demo';
catalog_name schema_name table_name tag_name tag_value
muh_catalog muh_demo demo_apply_tags use
muh_catalog muh_demo demo_apply_tags force
muh_catalog muh_demo demo_apply_tags kamino
muh_catalog muh_demo demo_apply_tags demo

I STILL WANT THE SOLUTION FOR APPLYING MACRO POST HOOK TO CONFIG AT PROPERTIES.YML LEVEL (exhibit 1A), so if anyone can solve this it would be great.
title: DBT post_hook macro with arguments in properties.yml
answer:
This was a bug, first reported in March 2023, related to non late-rendering behavior specifically in properties.yml files. The error message quoted was:

Could not render {{ my_macro() }}: 'my_macro' is undefined

To quote from the problem statement on the merged fix:

Because pre- and post-hooks within properties.yml files are not late-rendered for models, seeds, etc., references to {{ this }}, macros, etc. don't work.

The fix was merged 3 weeks ago and released for dbt-core 1.8.6. Looks like I can upgrade and put this behind me.
